iut_type: End Product (Smart Door Controller, antenna-connector module, Fulltech via Houdy)
customer_question: We want to put the Bluetooth logo mark on our product packaging/pamphlets and on the door unit itself — is there anything we need to be careful about?
question_variants: Where do we get an approved Bluetooth logo file to print on marketing materials?
Can we use any Bluetooth logo image we find, or must it come from a specific source?
actual_issue: Fulltech/Houdy mentioned they wanted to print the Bluetooth logo mark on their product and pamphlets for the Smart Door Controller, and Allion proactively addressed the correct logo usage requirement.
plain_english_explanation: Any Bluetooth logo printed on a product or its marketing materials must use the official electronic logo file distributed by Bluetooth SIG, not a recreated or independently sourced image.
consultant_answer: The Bluetooth logo mark used on products or pamphlets must be the official electronic file distributed by Bluetooth SIG. Allion attached the correct logo file set for use when preparing artwork.
decision_logic: Bluetooth SIG controls trademark usage of its logo; using anything other than the officially distributed file risks trademark non-compliance even if the product itself is properly certified.
final_recommendation: Whenever a customer mentions wanting to print the Bluetooth logo, proactively supply the official SIG logo file set rather than waiting to be asked, since using an incorrect logo image is an easy and common mistake.
risk_if_done_wrong: Using an unofficial or self-recreated Bluetooth logo image on packaging or marketing materials could violate Bluetooth SIG trademark usage requirements even if the underlying product registration is valid.
search_aliases: where to get Bluetooth logo file
